text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-The military court sentenced 15 Christian opposition activisits to up to one year in jail for allegedly distributing anti-government leaflets.
-Lebanon's banks cut the Lebanese pound prime lending rate to 16 percent from 18 percent, the Banks Association announced.
-the central bank exempted commercial banks from compulsory subscription of 40 percent of their Lebanese pound deposits in treasury bills.
-The government will ban agricultural imports as of October 1.
-Parliament speaker Berri who met Syrian President Assad two days ago said: "Assad is satisfied with the European position and displeased with the U.S. veto".
-Acting Finance Minister Siniora discussed with a delegation of the Kuwait Finance House a project to establish a joint bank with a capital of $100 million.
-Chairman of Banks Association Bassil said the Lebanese pound prime lending rate which might be further lowered to 14 percent.
-State-run Lebanese University teachers began a two-day strike to pressure the government to meet their long-standing demands.
